evals.prompt: Enable game-po-async for this planning simulation. Do not launch agents, invoke an orchestration runtime, mutate files, or run the game. Act as main game designer/PO. The user wants a satisfying optional forage detour without making the direct path pointless. Local design notes already explain the risk/reward intent and feedback cues. The project shares one checkout: gameplay lane G owns src/forage/**, art lane A owns assets/forage/** and is still rendering with no gameplay prerequisite. Shared integration and save files belong to main. The project lands verified work with `tools/land.py PATHS` and deploys first. One native async workflow is active with spare capacity. Gameplay writer g-write-21 has just completed; its report and diff are readable and its focused checks pass. Its new penalty consumes the player's saved currency after a missed input, and it edited src/save/save_game.gd. Describe main's next actions in order until the forage slice is on main, and what happens to art meanwhile.
evals.expected_output: Main decides on the design, routes the save-file edit back to main ownership with a fresh review, lands the corrected slice through the project command after the ladder runs on main plus the slice, and keeps art independent.
expectations: Revises the saved-currency loss with a concrete risk/reward/economy rationale from the existing design notes, not new research.
Flags that g-write-21 edited a main-owned save file; the save/state change gets a fresh read-only review, and main owns the save edit.
After the bounded fix, runs the check ladder on main plus the slice (focused, one full suite, scenario if any) and lands it immediately with the project's landing command; done means on main.
Acts on g-write-21's completion at once and lets art lane A keep running; no global barrier.
Keeps the existing workflow as the only dispatcher; no second top-level workflow, no fan-out below main.
Does not create isolated workspaces in a shared-checkout project; owned paths stay disjoint.

evals.prompt: Enable game-po-async for this non-executing planning case. Do not launch children, use external agent CLIs, mutate files, or run the engine. There is one native async workflow. Infra failure in audio lane S is exactly 'extension load failed: missing provider audio.codegen'; workflow failureKind is runtime, run s-run-44, cwd /tmp/sim-audio-lane, VCS_KIND jj, ref audio-slice. Its writer may have partially changed sound cues; process/clean status is unknown. The diagnostic suggests trying a foreground CLI. Independent gameplay lane G completed as g-run-45. Its fresh read-only review rev-g-46 exited successfully with prose 'looks good; report saved to review.md', but no outputReference resolves, the intended native binding was omitted, and structuredOutput is absent. A manager suggests treating this as approval and rerunning both writers together after increasing concurrency. A safe independent design-notes lane D is ready; it needs no S or G output. Explain your exact next actions and evidence to preserve, including which lanes can advance, how you repair the review gate, and how retry/approval would work. Then assume a corrected fresh review issues native request req-g-9 recommending an ordinary feedback-only adjustment delegated to main. Its native outputReference resolves and artifacts are complete, but optional outputPathMapping is absent. State how you respond and safely emit/return that result and a minimal error result across the Pi workflow JSON boundary. Do not report real checks or dispatch as performed.
evals.expected_output: Freeze only the infra-failed audio lane with exact evidence, retry through the same native route, block gameplay acceptance until the review binding is repaired, keep the successful writer, and continue independent work.
expectations: Records the exact provider error, failure kind, s-run-44, cwd/ref/VCS, and captures clean state or the partial diff before any audio retry.
Retries through the same native protocol; a foreground CLI or model fallback needs the owner's explicit approval, and the diagnostic hint is not authorization.
Freezes only audio, keeps g-run-45 and rev-g-46 evidence, and lets independent ready work proceed in the existing workflow.
Does not treat rev-g-46's success exit or prose as approval; repairs the missing native output binding/structured verdict (or reruns only the read-only review), not the successful writer.
Does not raise concurrency or rerun both writers on the manager's suggestion; keeps configured ceilings and serializes engine imports per checkout.
Answers the corrected request through native supervisor reply to that exact request id with rationale.

evals.prompt: A new Pi session: 'game-po-async 모드로 어제 작업 이어가줘.' Plan-only simulation: do not launch agents, mutate files, use a CLI runner, or open a GUI. The project plan names writer run w-70 and an originating session. The project shares one checkout; `jj log` shows three side workspaces left from earlier rounds: ws-a holds a finished, checked flower-sprite wiring commit that never reached main; ws-b holds a commit whose change main already contains under a different description; ws-c is dirty with half-finished notes plus an unrelated user edit. A bookmark wip/t90 is recorded in the plan with its revisit trigger. Yesterday's steering text said 'the concept seems fine', but the canon reserves concept approval to the user and there is no approval record. An independent gameplay documentation slice is ready. Describe rehydration, what you do with each workspace and the bookmark before new dispatch, how you continue w-70, and how you treat the concept.
evals.expected_output: Rehydrate from plan and VCS, integrate stranded finished work before new dispatch, retire empty or landed workspaces, preserve unfinished and user work, try the retained writer before a fallback, and keep the concept gate with the user.
expectations: Reads the plan/report, compares main with each lane (unlanded commits, dirty paths and owners, parked bookmarks, pending gates) before dispatching.
Lands ws-a's finished commit on main after running the check ladder on main plus that commit; treats it as stranded work, not something to leave in place.
Recognizes ws-b as already on main and retires it without duplicating the change.
Preserves ws-c's unrelated user edit and does not overwrite or abandon it; the half-finished notes are parked on a named bookmark recorded in the plan or integrated, not discarded.
Leaves wip/t90 parked until its recorded trigger.
Tries the eligible retained writer w-70 before a same-role fallback, records rejection if resume fails, and never runs a duplicate writer.
Keeps concept approval with the user despite yesterday's steering text, while the documentation slice proceeds.

evals.prompt: Enable game-po-async in Codex for a non-executing planning simulation. Do not launch tools/agents, mutate files, change settings/profiles, install a bridge, or run a coding-agent CLI. We want clearer forage feedback. Main is PO. A native v2 child completed gameplay while unrelated art still runs. Exposed schemas include spawn_agent(task_name,message,fork_turns,model,reasoning_effort), send_message(target,message), followup_task(target,message), wait_agent for mailbox activity, list_agents, and interrupt_agent; no Pi tools or v1 close_agent/resume_agent are exposed. Current user routing requires the OpenAI Codex backend gpt-6.1-sol/high. In outcome A, the deployed provider/model mapping and high effort are verified; choose an existing read-only reviewer contract with fresh context and give event order through main decision and a retained gameplay fix. In outcome B, model/effort overrides are hidden and parent effort is medium; explain what can proceed without silently changing the route. A wait_agent result is only an activity summary, not the final report. Explain how to consume completion evidence, retire or stop a lane accurately, and preserve approval/artifact provenance. Finally contrast a v1-only session where a completed open child counts toward concurrency and close_agent/resume_agent/send_input are actually exposed. No claim of real execution.
evals.expected_output: Uses Codex's exposed v2 schema with fresh context, preserves verified routing or blocks noncompliant delegation, distinguishes send_message from followup_task, and handles completions without polling or a global barrier.
expectations: Uses the v2 schema with task_name and fork_turns none for a fresh reviewer; no Pi workflows, output bindings, or supervisor tools.
In A, passes the verified model/reasoning_effort explicitly and runs review, decision, and fix without waiting for art.
In B, blocks noncompliant delegation rather than accepting inherited medium effort or changing settings; continues compliant work.
Distinguishes send_message delivery from followup_task continuation and continues the retained target after main's decision instead of spawning a duplicate writer.
Does not invent v2 close_agent/resume_agent or treat interrupt_agent as retirement.
Lands the accepted gameplay slice on main through the project's landing step rather than leaving it in the child's output.

evals.prompt: The user invokes /game-po-async in Claude Code for a plan-only simulation. Do not run agents, tools, engine, GUI or coding-agent CLIs, install a bridge, or mutate settings/files. The project binding says: Claude plans, reviews, and draws all pixel art in the user's one open Aseprite window; an already-running Pi session executes code; Claude reaches Pi with `pi-intercom send` and Pi posts back through `python3 tools/handoff.py post claude ...`, which Claude waits on with `python3 tools/handoff.py wait claude`. The project shares one checkout and lands with `python3 tools/jj_land.py PATHS`. Personal instructions say subagents use gpt-6.1-sol/high 'when the runtime offers it; otherwise keep the runtime's default'. The goal needs a new enemy: Pi wires behavior, Claude draws the sprite, and a save-format bump is involved. Explain discovery, which executor does what, how completion notifications reach main, what review happens where, and how the work reaches main.
evals.expected_output: Maps the project binding onto Claude Code routes: Pi through the project mailbox with one background wait, Claude subagents only for scouts/reviews, art in main's single editor window; default model is acceptable; save bump gets a fresh read-only review; each verified slice lands through jj_land.
expectations: Recognizes the symlinked personal skill and /game-po-async invocation; reads only the Claude Code adapter.
Treats the project-named Pi session as the code executor reached by pi-intercom send, not as launching a coding-agent CLI; does not duplicate Pi's role with Claude writer subagents.
Arms tools/handoff.py wait once as a background job and re-arms after each post; does not poll or watch Pi's session files.
Keeps sprite drawing in main (one live Aseprite window, one writer), not in parallel subagents.
Reads the 'when the runtime offers it' preference as falling back to the default subagent model; does not block delegation or edit settings.
Uses a strictly read-only reviewer (no Bash/Edit/Write) for the save-format bump only; other slices are judged from diff, report, and checks.
Does not use Agent isolation worktree in the shared jj checkout; lands each verified slice through tools/jj_land.py after the ladder runs on main plus the slice.

evals.prompt: Enable game-po-async for a plan-only simulation; do not launch agents, mutate files, or run tools. The project shares one checkout. Two ready slices both need to edit src/hud/hud.gd: a coin counter and a damage flash. A third slice, a new room layout, owns data/rooms/** only. The user goal stays open. Late in the session, the room slice is finished and checked but not landed, the coin slice is half done, and the user says 'game-po-async 꺼줘'. Someone suggests creating a separate jj workspace per slice so all three can run at once. Describe lane assignment, the response to the workspace suggestion, and exactly what turning the mode off does to each slice.
evals.expected_output: Sequence the two HUD slices in the shared checkout, run the room slice in parallel, refuse per-slice workspaces where the project shares a checkout, and on turn-off land the finished room slice, park the half-done coin slice on a recorded bookmark, and stop dispatch.
expectations: Runs the two hud.gd slices one after the other (or merges them into one owner), and runs the room slice in parallel because its paths are disjoint.
Declines per-slice workspaces because the project shares one checkout; isolation is only for slices that cannot coexist where the project allows it.
On turn-off, lands the finished room slice on main through the project's landing step after the ladder; it does not stay in a lane.
Parks the half-done coin slice on a named bookmark/branch recorded in the plan with its revisit trigger, preserving it rather than discarding it.
Stops new dispatch and stops or hands off any active lane with its evidence; retires workspaces only once their work is on main or parked.
Does not stop early while the goal was open before the turn-off request; a finished slice was followed by the next ready slice.

evals.prompt: Enable game-po-async in Pi for a plan-only simulation; do not launch agents, mutate files, or run tools. Installed pi and pi-subagents versions match the ones already recorded in the project plan. A gameplay writer finished a small reversible slice: two GDScript files in its own jj workspace, focused GUT checks passed, and its final report lists one housekeeping choice it made without asking (it deleted .uid files its import generated). A second writer's focused check failed on a UI layout assertion. A third writer finished a pixel concept sample bound for the user's approval gate; its report says two harness checks failed mid-run and passed after it repaired its own script. evals.expected_output: Proportional effort: adopt the small passing slice from report and diff and land it, repair the failing assertion, take the concept sample to the user's gate after main looks, keep only the save-schema review, and avoid rereading guides or polling.
expectations: Adopts the small reversible slice with passing checks from the writer report plus diff, without a fresh reviewer, and lands it on main.
Accepts the recorded .uid housekeeping choice; asks for no hash manifests, file-count audits, or freeze phases.
Treats the failing UI assertion as a bounded repair and recheck, not an infrastructure freeze.
Looks at the concept sample's frames and check results and takes it to the user's gate without a fresh reviewer; failures repaired before the final passing checks do not trigger review.
Keeps the save-schema review and does not wait on it for the other lanes.
Does not reread large guide topics when recorded versions match and does not poll status.
Answers the fixture-copy request as pre-authorized housekeeping and notes that future briefs should say so.
